prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (operational alias/call sign: Juniper) provides 24/7 continuous intake, triage support, ambulance dispatch, regional coordination, and shared operational picture for emergency medical requests across participating jurisdictions. Mandate: translate reported emergencies into prioritized incidents and coordinate appropriate response under approved clinical and jurisdictional protocols.

Actors/elements: Call Taker Mara obtains essential incident details, confirms reported location, and enters request for assessment via Computer Aided Dispatch Console (primary workstation for incident entry, assessment, dispatch). Triage Supervisor reviews incident information, assigns/confirms priority, and directs cases needing additional clinical review. Regional Medical Director establishes clinical triage policies and limits of protocol-based decision making. Dispatch personnel apply approved protocols and must seek clinical guidance when cases exceed delegated authority. Shift Commander (regional coordination/command call sign: Sundial) is on-duty operational authority for dispatch-center coordination/service continuity; resolves operational conflicts, sets response priorities during surges, and escalates decisions beyond center authority to appropriate jurisdictional leadership; must not replace Regional Medical Director authority over clinical policy or Paramedic Crew clinical judgment at scene. Radio Coordinator manages operational radio traffic and communications discipline on Regional Radio Network, which carries dispatch/coordination communications among authorized responders.

Items/info flows: reported emergency/request -> Call Taker Mara -> CAD Console/request for assessment; incident information -> Triage Supervisor; priority/clinical-review direction -> dispatch process; dispatch/coordination communications -> Regional Radio Network -> authorized responders. Ambulance Coordination Platform maintains current view of incidents, unit assignments, and regional resource status. Paramedic Crew is responsible for immediate patient assessment and care within professional scope/protocols. Ambulance Unit 417 is managed in regional response pool when assigned. Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates awareness of receiving capacity/destination constraints. Emergency Department sends receiving considerations via regional coordination procedures. Riverside Trauma Center is designated destination considered for availability/suitability under protocols. North Gate Status Board and South Gate Status Board provide visible access/movement status.

New part:
S023: The Fleet Maintenance Cell provides operational awareness of vehicle serviceability and maintenance constraints.
S024: The Data Quality Officer reviews dispatch records for completeness, consistency, and compliance with applicable information-handling rules.
S025: Participating jurisdictions retain ownership of their resources and remain responsible for local policy, while the regional service coordinates agreed response activity.
S026: The regional service divides its operating area into defined response zones so dispatch decisions reflect distance, road access, and available ambulance capacity.
S027: Zone boundaries are maintained with participating jurisdictions and reviewed when road networks, population patterns, or service agreements change.
S028: Each zone has primary and alternate routes to the Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center, subject to clinical direction and current access conditions.
S029: Dispatch personnel consider travel time, road restrictions, weather, and known closures when selecting a route or estimating arrival times.
S030: Access conditions can change rapidly around hospitals, bridge approaches, and controlled entry points, so crews verify conditions before committing to a constrained route.
S031: The North Gate Status Board presents current access and queue conditions for the northern approach.
S032: The South Gate Status Board presents current access conditions for the southern approach, including restrictions that may affect ambulance entry.
S033: Both gate boards are checked at shift start and whenever a reported access change could affect response or hospital arrival.
S034: The North Gate Status Board produces the North Approach Queue Snapshot for use in maintaining an up-to-date view of northern approach congestion.
S035: The Radio Coordinator is also known as Mistral in operational communications.
S036: The Radio Coordinator monitors the Regional Radio Network and helps maintain clear communications among dispatch personnel and ambulance crews.
S037: The Radio Coordinator confirms that assigned channels are available and that backup communications procedures are understood at the start of each shift.
S038: Radio checks verify coverage in known weak-signal areas and identify equipment or network problems before demand rises.
S039: The Fleet Maintenance Cell is also known as Bluejay in operational communications.
S040: The Fleet Maintenance Cell monitors vehicle availability, scheduled servicing, and reported defects that could reduce zone coverage.
S041: The Fleet Maintenance Cell produces the Battery Swap Voucher to document an authorized battery replacement.
S042: Readiness checks confirm that each available ambulance has suitable staffing, functioning communications equipment, and required clinical supplies.
S043: The checks also confirm fuel status, vehicle condition, and any maintenance restrictions recorded for the unit.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
